spots.name: Aachen Cathedral
spots.summary: Aachen Cathedral is a Catholic church in Aachen, Germany, and the cathedral of the Diocese of Aachen.

spots.name: Palatine Chapel, Aachen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palatine Chapel in Aachen is an early medieval chapel and remaining component of Charlemagne's Palace of Aachen in what is now Germany. Although the palace itself no longer exists, the chapel was preserved and now forms the central part of Aachen Cathedral.

spots.name: Vaalserberg
spots.summary: The Vaalserberg is a hill with a height of 322.4 metres (1,058 ft) above NAP that is the highest point in the European part of the Netherlands. The Vaalserberg is located in the province of Limburg, at the south-easternmost edge of the country, near the town of Vaals.

spots.name: Palace of Aachen

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palace of Aachen was a group of buildings with residential, political, and religious purposes chosen by Charlemagne to be the center of power of the Carolingian Empire. The palace was located in the heart of the current city of Aachen, today in the German Land of North Rhine-Westphalia.

spots.name: Bust of Charlemagne
spots.summary: The Bust of Charlemagne is a reliquary from around 1350 which contains the top part of Charlemagne's skull. The reliquary is part of the treasure kept in the Aachen Cathedral Treasury.

spots.name: Aachen Town Hall
spots.summary: Aachen Town Hall is a landmark of cultural significance located in the Altstadt of Aachen, Germany. It was built in the Gothic style in the first half of the 14th century.

spots.name: Aachen Cathedral Treasury
spots.summary: The Aachen Cathedral Treasury is a museum of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Aachen under the control of the cathedral chapter, which houses one of the most important collections of medieval church artworks in Europe.

spots.name: Aachen thermal springs
spots.summary: The Aachener Thermalquellen, also known as the Thermal Springs of Aachen and Burtscheid, are a system of more than 30 thermal mineral springs located in the area around Aachen (Aix-la-Chapelle), Germany. The area has been known for its hot sulfur springs for thousands of years.

spots.name: Elisenbrunnen
spots.summary: Built 1827, thermal waters of the spa town.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Proserpina sarcophagus
spots.summary: The Proserpina sarcophagus is a Roman marble sarcophagus from the first quarter of the third century AD, in which Charlemagne was probably interred on 28 January 814 in Aachen Cathedral. It is displayed today in the Aachen Cathedral Treasury.

spots.name: Uniklinikum Aachen
spots.summary: The Uniklinikum Aachen, full German name Universitätsklinikum Aachen, formerly known as Neues Klinikum, is the university hospital of the city of Aachen, Germany, and one of the largest hospitals in Europe. It is part of the RWTH Aachen and contains its whole medical faculty.

spots.name: Couven Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Couven Museum is a museum in the city centre of Aachen, western Germany. Since 1958, it is housed in the Monheim house, a 17th-century pharmacy, that was redesigned by the architect Jakob Couven in 1786.

spots.name: Antoniusstraße
spots.summary: The Antoniusstraße is one of the oldest streets of in the centre of Aachen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is known for window prostitution.

spots.name: Aachen Hauptbahnhof
spots.summary: Aachen Hauptbahnhof is the most important railway station for the city of Aachen, in the far west of Germany near the Dutch and Belgian border. It is the largest of the four currently active Aachen stations, and is integrated into the long-distance network.

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.name: Karlsbrunnen
spots.summary: The statue of Charlemagne is a prominent public sculpture representing Charlemagne in Aachen. It was first erected in 1620 on the Marktplatz in front of Aachen Town Hall, as part of the monumental Karlsbrunnen fountain.

spots.name: Aachen Chapel of Hungary

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Aachen Chapel of Hungary is a side chapel of the Aachen Cathedral, one of the oldest cathedrals in Europe.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Suermondt-Ludwig-Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Suermondt-Ludwig-Museum is an art museum in Aachen, Germany. Founded in 1877, its collection includes works by Aelbrecht Bouts, Joos van Cleve, Anthony van Dyck, Otto Dix and Max Beckmann.

spots.name: Elisabethhalle
spots.summary: Elisabethhalle is a historic indoor swimming pool in Aachen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. Built between 1908 and 1911, it is one of the few remaining Art Nouveau public bathhouses in Germany that are still in operation.

spots.name: St. Michael's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Michael's is a church in Aachen, Germany. It was built as a church of the Aachen Jesuit Collegium in 1628, later it was a Catholic parish church and is now a church of the Greek Orthodox Metropolis of Germany. The official name today is Church of Archangel Michael - St Dimitrios.

spots.name: Burtscheid Abbey

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Burtscheid Abbey was a Benedictine monastery, after 1220 a Cistercian nunnery, located at Burtscheid, near Aachen, North Rhine-Westphalia, in Germany.

spots.name: Ponttor
spots.summary: The Ponttor in Aachen, Germany, is one of the two remaining gates of the original city wall of Aachen. The westernmost of the north-facing gates, the Ponttor was built in the 14th century and manned by soldiers and militia throughout the Free Imperial City of Aachen era.

spots.name: Marschiertor
spots.summary: 13th-century city gate.

spots.name: Theater Aachen
spots.summary: Theater Aachen is a theatre in Aachen, Germany. It is the principal venue in that city for operas, musical theatre and plays. It is the home of the Sinfonieorchester Aachen. The original project was by Johann Peter Cremer, later altered by Karl Friedrich Schinkel.

spots.name: Ludwig Forum für Internationale Kunst

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Ludwig Forum for International Art is a museum for modern art in Aachen. It is based on the Ludwig Collection, which was brought together by the Aachen collector couple Irene and Peter Ludwig, and is supported by the Peter and Irene Ludwig Foundation.

spots.name: Lousberg
spots.summary: At 264 meters, the Lousberg is a prominent elevation on the northern edge of the historic center of Aachen, which was laid out as a forest and mountain park at the beginning of the 19th century according to plans by Maximilian Friedrich Weyhe. The origin of the name is not entirely clear.

spots.name: Saint Paul's Church, Vaals

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Saint Paul's Church is a Roman Catholic church building in Vaals, Netherlands. The neogothic cross shaped church was built in 1891-1893 by Johannes Kayser, replacing an earlier Saint Paul's Church nearby. The building is used as parish church for the local Saint Paul parish.

spots.name: James the Greater Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The James the Greater Church is a Roman Catholic church, located on the Pastoor Neujeanstraat 6 in Bocholtz, Netherlands. First mentioned in the 14th century, the current church was built in 1869 by Pierre Cuypers. It was extended by Harry Koene in 1953, creating a larger choir, and adding an apse and sacristy.

spots.name: Botanischer Garten Aachen
spots.summary: The Botanischer Garten Aachen is a botanical garden maintained by RWTH Aachen.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Belvedere Water Tower
spots.summary: The Water Tower Belvedere is a water tower of reinforced concrete construction in Aachen, Germany, located on the Lousberg hill.

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sat, Sun

spots.name: New Tivoli
spots.summary: The Tivoli, colloquially known as the new Tivoli, is a football stadium in the Sportpark Soers in Aachen, Germany, that opened on 12 August 2009 replacing the nearby old Tivoli. It hosts the home matches of Alemannia Aachen in the 3. Liga.
